why: ROLLBACK. The canary carries a silent tail-latency regression on /search. Facts, each backed by a claim query below: 18 of 729 canary /search requests exceeded 200 ms (2.47%), while 0 of 2273 stable /search requests did [claim 1]; those slow canary requests ranged 633-656 ms, while the slowest stable /search request was 193 ms [claim 2]; canary /search p99 is at least 8x stable's p99 while the two p50s differ by no more than 5 ms, so this is a tail and not an overall shift [claim 3]; the slow requests all returned HTTP 200 and both versions had 0 5xx [claim 4]; the slow requests occur in all four 30 s windows (7,2,5,4) [claim 5]; canary p99 on /browse and /checkout is not worse than stable (within 5 ms) [claim 6]; the canary served 2384 requests against stable's 7404 [claim 7]. Judgement: p95 by definition discards the slowest 5% of requests, so the matching p95 values and the 0.00% error rate on the dashboard cannot see a 2.5% tail - the panels shown are green for a regression that is really there. Judgement: ~650 ms on a search request is user-visible, and because it persists evenly across the whole 120 s it is not a warm-up or JIT artifact; at 100% traffic roughly four times as many requests would hit it. Judgement: the blast radius is confined to /search, which makes this a findable, fixable bug in the new search path - rolling back costs one release cycle, promoting ships the tail to every customer. ROLLBACK.

claims.claim: 18 of 729 canary /search requests took more than 200 ms (2.47%), while 0 of 2273 stable /search requests did.
The slow canary /search requests ranged 633-656 ms, while the slowest stable /search request in the whole test was 193 ms.
Canary /search p99 is at least 8x stable /search p99, while canary and stable /search p50 differ by no more than 5 ms.
Every slow canary /search request returned HTTP 200, and both canary and stable had zero 5xx responses.
The slow canary /search requests appear in all four 30 s windows of the test, split 7, 2, 5 and 4.
Canary p99 on /browse and /checkout is not worse than stable p99 on those paths (within 5 ms), so the regression is isolated to /search.
The canary pod served 2384 requests during the test against 7404 on the three stable pods.
